2) Formulation of diagnostic hypotheses and implementation of a diagnostic process organized with first-, second-, and third-level tests, balancing the information provided by the various investigations with their degree of invasiveness and cost
3) Formulation of the final diagnosis with hierarchical classification of the various issues and lifestyle and rehabilitation interventions
4) Formulation of the prognosis regarding life expectancy and quality of life

5) Establish an appropriate therapeutic strategy, including the correct dosage of appropriate medications and their possible combinations, assessing the benefit/risk and benefit/cost ratios, and any expected side effects

6) Knowledge of the atypical clinical presentation of the most common diseases in geriatric patients, the presence of comorbidities (multipathology), and differences in the clinical course and prognosis of diseases

7) Use of diagnostic and assessment protocols for frail and/or disabled multidimensional elderly patients and prescription of pharmacological combinations aimed at reducing iatrogenic risk in the elderly
8) Use of social and innovative rehabilitation care models (community medicine and primary care) to protect the socioeconomic and psychophysical health of the elderly
